4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: ROLLER mod v2 pushed to your repo by Sunday night: 1 bug report + 1 feature request filed as GitHub Issues on your partner's repo, your own bug fixed and your partner's feature request built (or scoped down with a written reason), both signed off by your partner, and a v1 → v2 changelog on your portfolio site.
4th Period.workingNow: Reproducing the bug your partner filed on you, fixing it in the right JavaScript file with Copilot, then triaging their feature request.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can reproduce the bug in my Issue, write a fix spec (rule → trigger → what changes), and push a fix that passes my own test by the end of class, so my game works the way I designed it.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.17 — Systematically test and refine programs using a range of test cases.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.6 — Reading closely literary and informational texts and viewing multimedia to determine how meaning is conveyed explicitly and implicitly through language.
agenda: Mini-lecture: The life of a bug + triage (7 min)
I do: reproduce → find the file → fix spec (6 min)
You do: reproduce and fix your bug with Copilot (22 min)
Triage the feature request: accept, scope, or decline (5 min)
Exit Ticket: comment on your Issue — fixed? proof? (5 min)
4th Period.connections: Yesterday you were the tester. Today you are the developer: you read the Issue filed on your repo, make the bug happen on purpose, find which JavaScript file it lives in, and fix it — then decide what to do with the feature request, the way real teams triage. Thursday you build that feature, after your partner confirms your fix.

6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Your finished game, published and embedded on your Google Site by Sunday night — with 1 bug report you wrote for a partner, 1 bug you fixed in your own game, and 3 sentences on what you changed and why.
6th Period.workingNow: Reading the bug report about your game, making the bug happen, and fixing it with Perplexity.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can make the bug from my report happen on purpose and fix it with Perplexity, so that by the end of class my game does what it should.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.17 — Systematically test and refine programs using a range of test cases.

agenda: Mini-lesson: Report → make it happen → fix → check (6 min)
I do: read a report, make the bug happen (5 min)
You do: make your bug happen, fix it with Perplexity (29 min)
Exit Ticket: Did your fix work? How do you know? (5 min)
6th Period.connections: Yesterday you found a bug in someone else's game. Today you get the report about YOUR game. First you make the bug happen on purpose — if you can't make it happen, you can't prove you fixed it. Thursday your tester checks your fix, and then you publish.
